purpose: desktop visual and real-time battle concept review

styles.label: A · 水墨写意
styles.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Deliver a finished high-quality desktop xianxia sect-management game ART DIRECTION PROTOTYPE, landscape 16:9, target 1792x1024. NOT a collage. The same comparison scene for five different art styles: a vast continuous Chinese mountain sect territory at human scale, seen from a fixed elevated three-quarter tactical camera at roughly 42 degrees. A substantial closed two-storey main hall stands in the upper central third; ancillary closed pavilions upper left and upper right. An expansive stone practice court occupies the middle and foreground, shaped natural grass banks and low rock terraces border it. A stream and usable broad stone bridge at the right; a long gently bending approach road enters bottom center; lateral paths continue left/right OUTSIDE THE FRAME so this feels like one view into a much larger traversable map, not a floating miniature island. Buildings are full-sized relative to adult people: doorway roughly 1.6 people tall, full main hall roughly eight people tall. Show 16 clear adult cultivator figures distributed in 4 loose groups on the court and paths, individually readable silhouettes in blue, ivory, muted ochre and dark red clothing. Characters occupy about 35-45px height at 1792px-wide image. Their grouping implies room for many simultaneous fights while this illustration is peaceful. Restrained foliage in coherent masses, deliberately designed paths and forecourts, 60 percent of frame is navigable space, no dense pebble noise or repetitive scattered bushes. Sky and distant peaks only the top 12 percent; ground-level tactical reading dominates. Cohesive lighting/materials between buildings, characters and landscape; carefully composed transitions and perspective, refined finished assets. No UI, text, labels, watermarks, logos, game title, borders. Style/medium: contemporary Chinese INK-WASH game art, confident expressive black/charcoal brush linework and restrained washes of indigo and vermilion on pale warm rice-paper color; distinct dry-brush edges and ink diffusion, very subtle paper grain. Elegant negative space, layered mist as depth outside the playable court; architectural contours and people remain crisp enough for gameplay. Buildings and stone pathways rendered through confident varying-width ink marks and soft flat wash, never photorealistic or shiny. Strong authored painting quality, not generic blue-green cartoon cel shading.
